display_name: Answer Validate Freeze Memorize Error Routine Blueprint
aliases: Show Project to AI recovery blueprint
description: Canonical cross-project continuation wrapper for answer, package, install, validate, Freeze, Error Memory review, and machine-enforced pre-output prevention of known operational regressions.
trigger_phrases: one zip install then validate same terminal block
when_to_load: When the user presses the Show Project to AI routine button or asks to continue current source/compact evidence through one update ZIP, chained install->validate execution, human-gated Freeze, and final Error Memory disposition.
when_not_to_load: Do not load for explanation-only work with no release, validation, Freeze, or Error Memory continuation.
do_not_regress: Embed the current selected Project and KANDA Reasoner Tool identities in the copied button text.
Keep all selected-Project source, staging, validation, Freeze, and Error Memory paths derived from the selected Project.
Keep canonical prompt source owned by the KANDA Reasoner Tool root.
Never deliver an isolated ZIP or claim installation as validation.
Before selecting the next action, derive the current lifecycle pointer for the exact current release identity.
For the same current release identity, never repeat a completed phase unless newer explicit evidence invalidates that phase or an earlier dependency.
Bind the last reliable marker to the current Project, feature, artifact or revision, and current source fingerprint when available.
Answer and emit work only for the first incomplete phase.
If identity or evidence conflicts, fail closed at the first unresolved phase without restarting the full lifecycle.
A new artifact, revision, fingerprint, or correction invalidates only downstream evidence that depends on the superseded identity.
Continue from the last reliable marker without requiring the user to retrain the AI.
Keep Preview read-only and Confirm and Write and Memorize Error explicitly human governed.
Never reintroduce deprecated router_bridge_patch_delivery_contract.
Every user-facing PowerShell code fence must be one independently pasteable unit.
Prefer direct packaged script invocation and never emit user-facing else, elseif, or finally clauses.
Require Windows PowerShell 5.1-compatible APIs unless a newer runtime is explicitly verified.
Use the exact current artifact path rather than an assumed destination or placeholder path.
Use current uploaded files, compact updates, local validation output, Freeze snippets, and Error Memory evidence as one continuation context.
Create one self-contained feature ZIP containing packaged installation and validation scripts.
Do not create standalone validation-report downloads or external runners without a named future consumer and retention owner.
Keep the Show Project to AI button linked to the canonical prompt path instead of copying prompt text into GUI source.
Create Error Memory lessons only after actual reusable failure evidence and duplicate checks; otherwise report NOT_REQUIRED.
Keep the Show Project to AI button dynamically linked to the canonical prompt path.

Require Fire Shield only when KANDA Reasoner or a KANDA-managed workflow is the actor touching an external Project; independent Project-owned IDE, terminal, CI, install, test, and validation work must not depend on KANDA selection, registry, portable runtime, Fire Shield, or Tool availability.
Deliver one paste-safe terminal block that invokes packaged INSTALL.ps1 and, only after successful Enter-Enter cleanup return, packaged VALIDATE.ps1.
Keep INSTALL.ps1 install-only and VALIDATE.ps1 validation-only even when one outer paste unit orchestrates both phases.
If installation fails, stop before validation; if validation fails, stop before Freeze.
After current VALIDATION OK and STATUS: IN_SYNC, prepare Freeze directly without asking for another validation command.
Evaluate Error Memory only after the validated Freeze is confirmed correct, and only for verified reusable non-duplicate failures.
